en: Oṃ, salutation to the Brahman that is Tat-Sat. Now begins the Devalasmṛti. Salutation to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
Now follows the description of expiation (prāyaścitta):
All the sages, having approached Devala—the best of sages—who was seated comfortably on the bank of the Sindhu river, spoke these words. (1)
O Blessed One, how indeed may Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras, led away by barbarians, attain purification again in their respective order? ||2||
How is bathing performed? How is purification? What should be the expiation? And what should be their conduct? Tell me that in detail. (3)
Devala said: One should avoid the region of Triśaṅku, extending twelve yojanas in every direction, to the north of the great river and to the south of Kīkaṭa.
O great sages, I shall now explain the expiation in detail.

In the case of female slaves or wives born of anuloma unions, the purification shall be equal to that of their master; however, when the master has died, it shall be that pertaining to blood relations.
By that brahmin who was led away by the barbarians, undrinkable liquor was drunk, forbidden food was eaten, and he committed incest with a woman who should not be approached. (7)
I shall declare its purification for up to one year:
for a Brahmin, it is proclaimed as the Cāndrāyaṇa together with the Parāka.
One *parāka* is for a Kṣatriya, joined with one-fourth of a *pādakṛcchra*; half a *parāka* is for a Vaiśya, and five days [of fasting] is for a Śūdra. (9)
One should cause the expiation to be performed for those who are devoid of nails and hair; for otherwise, there is indeed impurity for all four castes.
But when their bodies are devoid of the performance of expiation, the funeral rites must be performed for them by me, excluding the punishment of the wicked. (11)

If [the property] has been taken away by barbarians or seized by Śūdras, the punishment shall be [imposed] upon that wicked person; furthermore, all his rites, beginning with the purificatory consecrations, must be performed according to the rules.
And at the conclusion of the consecration rites for the Brahmins, those desiring purity should give a gift of a cow as a sacrificial fee, as well as horses, cattle, land, and gold. (13)
Only then does he attain the rank of those who have families, and not otherwise; by approaching his own wife according to the prescribed rule, he indeed becomes purified.
Now, if after a year he has been led away by barbarians, he becomes pure by bathing in the Gaṅgā once the penance has been performed. ||15||
Having gone to Sindhu, Sauvīra, and Saurāṣṭra, as well as to those dwelling in the borderlands, to Kaliṅga, Kauṅkaṇa, and Vaṅga, one becomes worthy of the purificatory rite. ||16||
And those who have been forcibly enslaved by Mlecchas, Cāṇḍālas, and bandits, and compelled to perform inauspicious deeds such as the slaughter of living beings like cows; ||17||
Likewise, the wiping away of leavings, eating from that same vessel, and the consumption of the flesh of donkeys, camels, dogs, and boars. ||18||
Likewise, for associating with their women or eating together with them,
the purification for a twice-born man who has lived thus for a month is the Prājāpatya penance.
For one who has maintained the sacred fires, however, there shall be either the Cāndrāyaṇa or the Parāka penance;
or, having lived for a year [in violation], he should perform both the Cāndrāyaṇa and the Parāka.
A Śūdra who has lived [in the house] for one year should drink barley-gruel for half a month;
a Śūdra who has lived there for one full month is purified by a quarter-kṛcchra penance. ||21||
After one year, an expiation may be prescribed by the best of the twice-born;
after four years, he attains that state [of purity].

For that evil-minded person for whom no reduction [of sin] is found and for whom there is no atonement, the shaving of the hair on the secret parts, the armpits, the head, and the eyebrows must be performed. 23.
Having commenced the penance, one should indeed perform the penance;
one should bathe three times a day, wearing clean clothes and with senses subdued. (24)
With Kuśa grass in hand, one should be devoted to truth; for it has been declared by Devala that [this practice lasts] for a year, or half a year, or even a month, or half a month. (25)
What is the purification for one who has been carried off by force by barbarians?
For a Śūdra who has lived [among them] for a year, purification is indeed by means of the Cāndrāyaṇa penance.
For a six-month period, one should perform the Parāka penance; for three months, half a Parāka;
and for a month, a Pādakṛcchra, while keeping the nails and hair untrimmed. ||27||

One should cause a Kṣatriya to perform three-quarters of the prescribed penance, a Vaiśya half, and one should cause a Śūdra to perform one-quarter of the penance prescribed for a twice-born man. ||28||
At the conclusion of the penance, a milch cow is considered the prescribed sacrificial fee;
likewise, he who sits within the household compound does not incur sin. ||29||
A child under sixteen years of age, as well as one who is eighty years old,
women, and the sick, deserve only half of the prescribed penance.
For one who is less than eleven years old and more than five years old,
the brother, the father, or another guardian shall perform the penance.
One should personally observe all the vows; otherwise, one is not purified at all.
One should perform the *tila-homa* sacrifice and recite prayers with diligence. (32)

Sin is transmitted among men through conversation, touch, shared breath, traveling together, sitting together, eating together, officiating at sacrifices for them, teaching them, and sexual union. (33)

By performing a sacrifice for one who is fallen, by forming a matrimonial alliance with one, by studying the Veda together with one, or by eating in the company of one, a person falls immediately; of this there is no doubt.

By associating with an outcast for a year— performing acts such as officiating at his sacrifices, sitting with him, or sacrificing for him— one falls from one's status, even if one was previously capable of fulfilling all desires.
Hereafter, I shall proclaim this auspicious expiation for women who have been forcibly led away by barbarians and have, at some point, undergone sexual intercourse.
When a Brāhmaṇī, a Kṣatriyā, a Vaiśyā, or a Śūdrā has been abducted by outcastes, what kind of expiation is prescribed as being just for the Brāhmaṇī? ||37||
If a Brāhmaṇī woman feeds a Mleccha, or if she eats what is unfit to be eaten, her purification is by means of a Parāka penance; for each subsequent [offense], the penance increases by one-quarter.
Sexual intercourse was not committed with them, nor was anything unfit for consumption ever eaten; purification then occurs after three nights, even if food from Mlecchas has been consumed. (39)

When a woman in her courses has been touched by a Mleccha or by another [unworthy person], she becomes pure after staying for three nights and bathing with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||40||
If a Brāhmaṇa woman and a Kṣatriya woman, both in their menses, touch one another,
their purification shall occur after three nights, according to the word of Devala.
If a Brāhmaṇa woman and a Śūdra-born woman touch each other while in their menses, she becomes pure by fasting for five nights and consuming the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||42||

A Brāhmaṇa woman should perform fasting; a Kṣatriya woman should perform a bath with her clothes on; for women of the Vaiśya caste, eating at night is prescribed; and for a Śūdra woman, it is ordained [to eat only] at night. 43.
Eating the food of Mlecchas, physical contact with Mlecchas, or dwelling together with Mlecchas for one year—or even beyond a year—one becomes pure after three nights of fasting. ||44||
And for those traveling through wildernesses who have been seized by barbarians or thieves, having eaten either edible or inedible food out of hunger or fear; ||45||

Having returned again to his own country, expiation for the four castes is as follows: a Brāhmaṇa should perform one *kṛcchra* penance, a Kṣatriya should perform half of that, a Vaiśya should perform three-quarters, and a Śūdra is purified by a quarter.
If a woman is forcibly seized by Mlecchas and treated as a Guru’s wife, she does not attain purification through the rite for a Guru’s wife; another [woman] becomes pure after three nights. ||47||
A woman—whether she be a Brāhmaṇī, a Kṣatriyā, a Vaiśyā, a Śūdrā, or one of another caste—who conceives from a Mleccha, whether out of desire or unintentionally, [is subject to this rule]. (48)
If she should consume forbidden food, how may her purification be achieved?
Purification consists of the Sāntapana Kṛcchra penance and the heating of the womb with clarified butter. (49)
A woman into whose womb an embryo is cast by one of a different caste remains impure as long as the fetus has not been expelled. (50)
Once the fetus has been expelled, or even upon the appearance of the menses, that woman is then purified, like stainless gold. (51)
That embryo may be given to another, but it must never be taken by oneself; for one should avoid giving it to someone of one's own caste, lest there be a confusion of castes (*saṃkara*) otherwise.
For one who has been forcibly seized by barbarians for five, six, seven,
or up to ten, twenty years, purification is prescribed.
For him, this purification consisting of two Prājāpatya penances is prescribed;
beyond this there is no purification for one who has lived together [with the sinner] even for a single Kṛcchra.
For one who has lived among Mlecchas for twenty years, starting from five, this purification is declared: two Cāndrāyaṇas.
Having first shaved the hair of the armpits, the private parts, the head, the beard, and the eyebrows, he should then remove the nails and hair of his hands and feet; thus he becomes pure. 56.
That best of the twice-born who does not know how to grant an expiation, yet gives purification to another, eats that which is impure because of his own lack of purity. //57//
If one sits in an assembly or touches a Mleccha, or even dwells together with one, one should perform a bath with one's clothes on and observe a fast for one day. ||58||
A mother or a father may somehow become a barbarian; yet there is no impurity for one who has lost [his caste], according to the word of Devala.
The son should likewise abandon his mother and father,
and thereafter offer the remaining funeral cake (piṇḍa) to his grandfather.

For women, for Śūdras, and likewise for those who have fallen from their caste, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) should not be given; it should be given, however, without the accompaniment of mantras.
Varuṇa is the deity in urine; Havyavāhana (Agni) in cow dung; Soma in milk; Vāyu in curd; and Ravi (the Sun) is declared [to be the deity] in ghee. ||62||
Cow’s urine from a copper-colored cow, cow dung from a white cow, milk from a golden-colored cow, and curd from a blue cow; //63//
Ghee indeed possesses the color black; water has the range of all colors; whose color would not be perceived? ||64||
Cow’s urine and cow dung should each be six mātrās, and water with kuśa grass three mātrās; ghee and milk should be ten mātrās each, and curd should be ten mātrās. ||65||

In the case of a religious vow, however, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) must be administered by those who expound the Veda as the prescribed penance for all castes according to the specified number. ||66||
If, however, one should cause [the gift] to be given otherwise, that twice-born man would be liable for penance. ||67||
He who drinks the milk of a tawny cow while it is being drawn, warm from the stream, performs this *kṛcchra* penance composed by Vyāsa; it purifies even a dog-eater.
One should perform an oblation of sesame seeds and recite prayers without weariness;
by means of the mantra "viṣṇo rarāṭam," the one who has performed penance becomes purified. ||69||
What is the use of saying more here? An oblation of sesame seeds is prescribed;
by giving sesame seeds and eating sesame seeds, one should effect the removal of sins. (70)
Whatever bath, merit of sacred fords, or austerity the Brahmins accomplish, that very thing proceeds toward him who has committed sin; its fruit is produced for him.
The expiation has been declared by Devala as it was stated;
you ought not to disregard the words of the other sages otherwise. (72)
One who performs penance should attain purification by bestowing gifts of gold, cows, land, and daily fodder for cattle upon Brahmins. (73)
If one has lived together for five days, one is purified by not conversing with them, not eating with them, consuming the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and giving a gift. ||74||
If a preeminent twice-born man should dwell among the Mlecchas for one, two, three, or four years, either in succession or due to the acquisition of wealth; ||75||
For one day he should consume cow urine; for three days, cow dung; for three days, combined with milk; and on the fourth day, mixed with curd.

On the fifth day, one should cause the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) mixed with ghee to be offered; this should continue for fifteen days, seventeen days, fifteen days, and twenty days. ||77||
I shall now declare the rules for cohabitation and the purification of the bodies of the twice-born:
for a period of five days, one should consume the five products of the cow (pañcagavya); for a period of ten days, it shall be the pādakṛcchra penance.
The *parāka* penance lasts fifteen days, and the *atikṛcchra* twenty; he for whom the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) enter his stomach according to the prescribed rule [is purified]. (79)
Whatever evil deed has been committed, all of it is destroyed for that embodied being after five,
seven, eight, ten, twelve, or even twenty days; for a Brahmin who has been taken away by Mlecchas, the purification is through the *pañcagavya*.
Having consumed the five products of the cow—cow’s milk, curd, urine, ghee, and milk—one should fast on the following day; thus one performs the Sāṃtapana Kṛcchra penance. ||81||
A separate *sāṃtapanam* consists of six days with various substances followed by a fast;
this *kṛcchra* performed over seven days is known as the *mahāsāṃtapana*.
When the leaves of the *parṇa*, *udumbara*, *rājīva*, and *bilva* trees, along with *kuśa* grass water, are drunk individually every day, it is declared to be the *pūrṇakṛcchra* penance. ||83||
One should drink each of these—hot milk, ghee, and water—daily for one day, followed by a fast for one night; this is the purifying *taptakṛcchra* penance. (84)
Eating once a day, eating only at night, likewise eating only what is unasked for, and fasting for one day—this is declared to be the *pādakṛcchra* (one-quarter penance). ||85||
The Kṛcchrātikṛcchra consists of subsisting on milk for twenty-one days;
the Parāka is proclaimed to consist of fasting for twelve days. ||86||
The consumption of oil-cake, potherbs, buttermilk, water, and barley-meal on successive days, followed by a fast for one night, is proclaimed as the *kṛcchra* known as *saumya*. ||87||
Through the practice of each of these for three nights in successive order, this is to be known as the "tulāpuruṣa" [vow], which lasts for fifteen days. ||88||

One should eat morsels equal in size to a peahen's egg, increasing them according to the lunar days during the bright fortnight; one should decrease the morsels by one each day during the dark fortnight—thus one performs the Cāndrāyaṇa Kṛcchra penance.
"In whatever manner there may be two hundred and forty morsels"—thus is proclaimed the Dharmaśāstra composed by Devala. (90)
This Devalasmṛti is completed.
